# mux

> mux is a command-line tool that copies and syncs files between folders, web addresses and other machines. One command on each side sends a folder between two machines, through home routers, with every chunk checked against a BLAKE3 digest. It runs on Linux, macOS and Windows, and is open source (MIT).

This page describes release 0.3.0. Progress and notes for people go to standard error. What a command produced goes to standard output. Every command takes `--json`, which writes one JSON object on each line of standard output.

## Install

- macOS or Linux: `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuvichh/mux/main/install.sh | sh` puts `mux` in `~/.local/bin`. `MUX_INSTALL=/some/folder` names another folder, and `MUX_VERSION=v0.3.0` another release.
- Homebrew: `brew install yuvichh/tap/mux`
- Windows: download `mux.exe` from https://github.com/yuvichh/mux/releases/latest

## Commands

- `mux cp <SOURCE>... <DESTINATION>` copies. A source is a file, a folder, a web address or a ticket. The destination is a folder, written with a `/` at its end if it is not there yet, or `peer:`.
- `mux cp ./folder peer:` offers a folder to other machines. It prints one ticket (a line that begins `mux://`) on standard output and runs until it is stopped. Keep it running while the other machine fetches.
- `mux cp 'TICKET' ./downloads/` fetches what a ticket names into `./downloads/`. Run it again to carry on after a break. Quote the ticket: it holds `?` and `&`.
- `mux cp https://example.org/file.iso ./downloads/` downloads from the web. `--hash sha256:<64 hex>` or `--hash blake3:<64 hex>` checks the file. `--mirror <URL>` reads the same file from a second server at once.
- `mux sync <SOURCE> <DESTINATION>` makes the destination match the source and fetches only what changed. The source is a folder, a web address or a ticket. `--dry-run` says what would change. Nothing is removed without `--delete`. What is replaced or removed goes to `.mux-trash` inside the destination unless `--no-trash` is given. A sync that would remove more than half of the destination stops unless `--force` is given.
- `mux probe <PLACE>` says what is at a web address, a folder or a ticket, and copies nothing.
- `mux id` prints this machine's node id.

`--dry-run` works on `cp` and `sync`. `--no-relay --listen <ADDR>` makes two machines connect at an address and through no relay.

## Standard output

Without `--json`, a finished copy writes one line: the path that was written, a tab, the size in bytes, a tab, and `verified`, `consistent` or `already there`.

With `--json`, each line has `"v":1` and an `event`:

- `start`: `source`, `destination`, `bytes`, `files`
- `progress`: `bytes`, `of`
- `file`: `path`, when a file is whole and has its final name
- `done`: `path`, `bytes`, `checked`, `fetched`, `kept`
- `plan`: what `--dry-run` would copy
- `offer`: `ticket`, `name`, `bytes`, `files`, when something is offered
- `step`, `synced`, `sync_plan`: what a sync does or would do
- `probe`: the answer of `mux probe`
- `error`: `code`, `kind`, `message`, `hint`. It is the last line of a command that failed.

## Exit codes

- 0: done
- 1: failed for a reason not listed here
- 2: the command line is wrong. Running it again will not help.
- 3: nothing is at the source
- 4: the source could not be reached or stopped sending. Run the same command again: it carries on with what it stored.
- 5: the source changed while it was read. Run the same command again.
- 6: what arrived does not have the digest that was given
